title: 0% battery warning can be shown when reported battery level briefly drops and then returns to normal
line: A battery level that drops to 0% for just a moment no longer shows the critical battery warning or starts the hibernate countdown.
explanation: Powerdevil reacted to every drop in the battery level reported by UPower right away. A dying battery can make UPower report 0% for a fraction of a second before returning to its real level, and that single reading was enough to show the "Battery Critical (0% Remaining)" notification with a 60-second hibernate countdown. Now a drop starts a 5-second timer, and the low or critical warning is only shown if the level is still below the threshold when it fires; increases are still handled immediately.

commits.message:
daemon: Wait a few seconds before warning about a battery drop

A dying battery can make UPower report 0% for an instant before going
back to its real level, and that was enough to show the critical battery
warning and start hibernating. Only warn if the drop lasts five seconds.

BUG: 518023

media.caption: UPower reports 0% for 0.7 s while the battery is at 57%: the critical warning with the hibernate countdown appears
Same 0.7 s blip to 0% with the fix: no warning
Recording of the blip: the critical warning flashes up and disappears
Recording of the same blip with the fix: nothing appears

reviews.text: Debouncing brief UPower battery percentage drops in PowerDevil::Core is the right layer and direction for this bug, and the before/after evidence reproduces the reporter's 0% blip well. However, starting a single 5-second timer on every drop without resetting, stopping on recovery, or clearing on AC plug-in and battery removal introduces several real edge-case bugs that can bypass the debounce or emit spurious critical warnings.
changes: Do not start m_batteryDropTimer on non-threshold drops (e.g., 57% -> 56%), or stop it on recovery and restart it when crossing into a lower threshold; otherwise a 0% blip occurring near the end of an earlier 1% drop's 5-second window (or within 5 seconds of a recovered blip) fires almost immediately without waiting 5 seconds.

Stop m_batteryDropTimer in Core::onAcAdapterStateChanged when state == BatteryController::Plugged; otherwise dropping to a critical level on battery and plugging in AC within 5 seconds still fires the timer with NotifyWhenAcPluggedIn and pops up a delayed critical/hibernate warning after AC is connected.

Guard the m_batteryDropTimer timeout callback against m_batteriesPercent.isEmpty() (and/or stop the timer in Core::onDeviceRemoved when no power-supply batteries remain), because removing the last battery during the 5-second window makes currentChargePercent() return 0 and triggers a bogus 0% critical warning.

reviews.text: Debouncing drops in Core::onBatteryChargePercentChanged is the right place and matches Nate's suggestion; passing an empty udi is safe because only peripheral batteries use it, and the dbusmock before/after plus the lasting-drop regression checks are convincing. But the timer is never stopped when the level comes back: it keeps running from the first blip, so a second blip that starts shortly before it fires (e.g. 0% at t=0-0.5 s, again at t=4.8 s) is read at t=5 s and still shows the critical warning and hibernate countdown. That is exactly the repeated-blip pattern a dying battery produces. Also, an open low-battery notification now only updates its percentage when the timer fires instead of on every drop.
changes: In the currentPercent > previousPercent branch, stop m_batteryDropTimer once the level is back at or above m_percentBeforeBatteryDrop, so every new drop gets its own full 5 s window (or restart the timer on each drop and keep the original 'before' level).
Keep calling updateBatteryNotifications(currentPercent) right away on drops so an already-open low/critical notification still shows the live percentage.
Re-test with two blips about 4.5 s apart and confirm nothing appears.
